cycles.method: static: tools/build/cycle_count.py (--verify: the marker is a no-op), the per-sample loop with the bucket tick taken and HPF on, 378 cycles/sample. measured: perf.py bench, benchmark_reverbs.run as benchmark_stock_dsp.py runs it (one instance per core at positions 0 and 4, audio at X:0, 4,096 blocks of 16 frames, the null stub's peak subtracted) on the private native image carrying BBD in the space of SPRING REV and PLATE REV (e648cee0..., the 0.1.1 card build). Worst of the BBD cases: the dearest settings with a trig split, 399.31 executed instructions/sample (363.06 unsplit, 326.44 at the defaults; 0.1.0: 439.44). Executed instructions in dsp_host, not chip cycles; no stalls modelled.

stock.baseline: perf.py bench: SPRING REV, CHORUS and DJ EQ run on the stock image through the same cases as BBD (fixed, the moving pattern, a trig split at every position 1-15). Its unsplit figures reproduce out/stock_dsp_bench/results.json exactly (SPRING REV 257.5, CHORUS 253.62, DJ EQ 293.38).
stock.justification: BBD runs a whole bucket-brigade chain per sample: a 2:1 feedback compressor whose divide (24 steps, the Pade tanh folded in) runs every sample, an 8th-order Butterworth anti-alias and a 7th + 2nd order reconstruction filter (eight biquads and a real pole, about 90 words of the loop) that track the clock, the clocked bucket line with a charge-transfer polynomial and noise, a DC blocker, the expander, the feedback tilt (a split and a bandpass) and a soft output stage. Under the same cases, trig splits included, its worst case 439.44 is 1.50x CHORUS (293.06, the closest stock effect: a BBD-style modulated line), 1.40x SPRING REV (314.19, the cost target for new FX) and 1.33x DJ EQ (330.94, the dearest stock effect); unsplit 405.00 against 253.62, 257.50 and 293.38. Earlier passes cut the cost: FDBK and TONE glide once a call, one filter section follows the clock per call instead of all nine, and a bookkeeping pass with bit-identical output. Going further means lower filter orders, which changes the sound. Four per core are 4 x 378 = 1,512 of the 3,120 usable static cycles. That leaves 1,608 for the four FX1 effects on those tracks and any other module on the core; the stress run with CHORUS on every FX1 peaked at 2,697.9 executed instructions per sample per core. Real-chip headroom beside heavy FX1 effects is unmeasured. The worst case has the SETUP high-pass HPF on (a clock-independent 2-pole section with error feedback, rebuilt each call while on); HPF 0, its default, branches around it.

stress.method: perf.py stress (E-Verb's load, adapted). stress_project.py needs an Octatrack template project, which is not available here, so the same load is driven straight into dsp_host on the private native image (the 0.1.1 card build, e648cee0...): BBD on FX2 of all eight tracks (four per core) behind CHORUS on every FX1 (eight named slots; DJ EQ, the dearest stock effect, has five); per block, three LFOs (sine, triangle, square) on BBD's TIME, FDBK and MIX, and a new random value on every named slot of both effects each sixteenth at 120 BPM: 17 slots changed per step, of which 12 can be locked on a unit (BBD's six main-page knobs and CHORUS's six; STGS, LIM, HPF and CHORUS's TAPS and FBLP are SETUP knobs that change only with Parts on a unit, so this changes more than locks can and repeatedly forces BBD's fade-and-clear); unnamed slots keep their defaults (BBD's hidden slot 11 at 127); trig splits of 1, 3, 7, 8, 12 and 15 frames on six tracks; eight different 32 s stems plus a 2 s tail; dsp_host -guard 0x4000 -guard-shared -dirty 0x5a. Result: no hang; BBD's eight instances 0 stray writes and 0 clobbers, and no instance clobbers another (the guard also counts 13320219 stray-write regions for the stock CHORUS instances, not examined further); per-core peak 2821.7 and 2831.3 executed instructions/sample with all sixteen effects. It exercises the DSP side only: the firmware's own LFO and lock delivery, Part switches and the ColdFire side are not in it. 0.1.1: 2 s of audio (104 s of host time), the audit minimum since 15 October 2026 (0.1.0 ran 32 s).
